final_answer: When an mRNA vaccine is injected, it introduces a piece of genetic material called mRNA into the body. This mRNA contains instructions for making a protein found on the surface of a virus, such as the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2. Once inside the body, the mRNA is taken up by cells, which use it to produce the viral protein. These proteins are then displayed on the surface of the cells, acting as a signal to the immune system. The immune system recognizes the protein as foreign and mounts a response, producing antibodies and memory cells. If the person is later exposed to the actual virus, the immune system can quickly recognize and fight it off, preventing illness. This process creates immunity without causing the disease.
